newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan stocks depository to begin in July.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan stocks depository to begin in July.

text.p: Pakistan's Central Depository Company (CDC), which is to set up a central depository system for the stock market, has said it would start its business operations from July.
CDC chief executive Najam Ali told reporters in Karachi that all the legal and technical snags in share transcations through a central depository system had been removed.
Analysts said a central depository system would provide transparent and efficient transactions through a computerised book entry system.
Ali said that by June 1998 50 companies' stocks would be traded through the CDC.
The CDC would eliminate the present need to count, verify, store and transport share certificates and reduce their transfer time to a few days instead of at least 45 days now, he added.

The CDC is owned by Pakistan's Karachi, Lahore and Islamabad stock exchanges, Citibank, the International Finance Corporation, the Muslim Commercial Bank, Habib Bank Ltd, National Investment Trust, the Investment Corporation of Pakistan and Pakistan Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation.
